description: Send Wake-on-LAN magic packets to a configured host and, by default, wait until it answers on its TCP check port. Name the host by its alias from wol_list_hosts; the MAC, broadcast address, and ports come from the operator's profile, and a host this machine has no interface on (on_segment false in wol_list_hosts) is refused before anything is sent. It probes the check port once, sends 3 packets, then re-probes every 2 seconds until the port answers or wait_for_s elapses. The result state is already_awake (the port answered before the packets went out; they are still sent), awake (it answered within the window, with time_to_answer_ms), not_reachable (the window elapsed; the host may still be booting, so re-check with wol_check_host), or unverified (no probe ran: wait_for_s was 0, or the profile has no address).

wait_for_s.description: Seconds to wait for the host's check port to answer after the first packet (0–55, default 30). 0 sends and returns without checking. 55 is the cap so the whole call fits inside the 60-second request timeout many MCP clients apply; re-check a slow cold boot with wol_check_host.

name: wol_wake_host

broadcast.description: Broadcast address the packets went to.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock time for the whole call, in ms.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unknown_host`: The alias matches no configured profile. `off_segment`: The profile's broadcast address (configured or derived) is not the directed broadcast of any local interface, or no broadcast can be derived. Nothing is sent. `wake_in_progress`: Another wol_wake_host call for the same host is still running; one wake per host runs at a time. Nothing is sent. `socket_error`: Binding the UDP socket, enabling broadcast, or sending a packet failed. A partial send fails the call too; the error data carries how many packets went out. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

guidance.description: Next step, present when state is not_reachable or unverified.

interface.description: Local network interface the packets were sent from.

local_address.description: Local IPv4 address the socket bound to.

mac.description: MAC address the packets carried, lowercase colon form.

packets_sent.description: Magic packets sent (always 3 on a returned result).

probe.description: Probes of the host's check port; present unless state is unverified.

address.description: Host address probed, as configured (hostname or IP).

attempts.description: Probes made, counting the one before the packets.

last_outcome.description: Outcome of the last probe. open: connected. refused: the machine answered but nothing listens on the port. no_answer: nothing answered within the probe timeout.

secureon_set.description: Whether the profile's SecureOn password was appended to the packets (never the password itself).

state.description: already_awake: the check port answered before the packets went out (they were still sent). awake: it answered within the window. not_reachable: the window elapsed without an answer; the host may still be booting. unverified: no probe ran (see unverified_reason).

time_to_answer_ms.description: Time from the first packet to the confirmation poll that connected, in ms. Polls run every 2 seconds, so this is an upper bound on when the check port started answering, not the exact moment. Present only when state is awake.

unverified_reason.description: Why no probe ran. wait_disabled: wait_for_s was 0. no_address: the profile has no address (reported when both apply). Present only when state is unverified.

wol_port.description: UDP destination port the packets were sent to.

title: Wake Host
